games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct verb after an indefinite pronoun?
choices: Everyone is ready for the presentation.
Everyone are ready for the presentation.
rounds.answer: Everyone is ready for the presentation.
rounds.explanation: Everyone is singular, so it takes the singular verb is. The other three sentences pair a singular pronoun with a plural verb.

rounds.prompt: What does the word burrow mean?
choices: A large area of land ruled by one government
A very bright light that is hard to see in
A hole or tunnel that an animal makes in the ground to live in
A written agreement between two or more groups
rounds.answer: A hole or tunnel that an animal makes in the ground to live in
rounds.explanation: A burrow is an animal home dug into the ground. The other options define empire, glare and contract.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses anyone correctly?
choices: Anyone left a bag in the hall.
Anyone has been using the tablets today.
Anyone is more important than teamwork.
rounds.answer: Did anyone see my notebook?
rounds.explanation: Anyone belongs in questions and negatives. The other three are statements, which need someone, somebody or nothing.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence avoids a double negative?
choices: Nobody was not late for class.
There is not nothing in the box.
I can't find nothing in my bag.
rounds.answer: Nobody was late for class.
rounds.explanation: Nobody already carries the negative, so no extra not is needed. The other three sentences say the opposite of what the writer meant.

rounds.prompt: According to The Night Sky Above Us, in which year was the first artificial satellite launched?
rounds.explanation: The passage dates the launch of Sputnik 1 to 1957. The Moon landing came in 1969, twelve years later.

rounds.prompt: Which unit word describes somebody who feels sleepy and wants to rest?
rounds.answer: drowsy
rounds.explanation: Drowsy means sleepy. Loyal describes faithfulness, towering describes height and booming describes loudness.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: What did the early observers build on high ground, and what did they use it for?
choices: They built observatories on high ground so that they could map the patterns of the stars.
They built a towering windmill from card and wire, and Leo claimed the glare from the bulbs proved it worked.
They kept improving the sensor after it failed, and on fair day both the burrow and the sensor worked perfectly.
rounds.answer: They built observatories on high ground so that they could map the patterns of the stars.
rounds.explanation: The first paragraph lists observatories, star maps and brass measuring instruments as the observers' tools.

rounds.prompt: What did Amal's team build for the science fair, and what did the model show?
choices: He believes that nobody should sign anything they have not read, so he wants the figures first.
It says that nothing in science happens quickly, so you have to be patient to get brilliant results.
They built a model burrow that showed how a rabbit lives inside an animal home.
rounds.answer: They built a model burrow that showed how a rabbit lives inside an animal home.
rounds.explanation: Amal explains the project to the visitors crowding round her table in the opening lines.

rounds.prompt: Why does Sami want to research the plastic-cup boycott before he joins it?
choices: Scientists began to cooperate across borders, sharing ideas and instruments as they worked towards the Moon.
He believes that nobody should sign anything they have not read, so he wants the figures first.
Its measurements of position and brightness were so accurate that nobody had produced anything as complete.
rounds.answer: He believes that nobody should sign anything they have not read, so he wants the figures first.
rounds.explanation: Sami states this reason himself, and the team then asks the group leader to show them his figures.

rounds.prompt: The passage calls the rockets towering. What does that word tell you about them?
choices: It tells you the rockets are extremely tall, which is why the writer calls them marvels of engineering.
Its measurements of position and brightness were so accurate that nobody had produced anything as complete.
There is no shop in space and nobody can rush up with a spare part, so the crew repair things themselves.
rounds.answer: It tells you the rockets are extremely tall, which is why the writer calls them marvels of engineering.
rounds.explanation: Towering means very tall or high, and the praise for the engineering sits in the same sentence.

rounds.prompt: Elena tells the team they seem very loyal to their work. Which detail from the story supports her?
choices: It tells you the rockets are extremely tall, which is why the writer calls them marvels of engineering.
They built observatories on high ground so that they could map the patterns of the stars.
They kept improving the sensor after it failed, and on fair day both the burrow and the sensor worked perfectly.
rounds.answer: They kept improving the sensor after it failed, and on fair day both the burrow and the sensor worked perfectly.
rounds.explanation: Loyal means staying with something you care about, and this team stayed with equipment that had already failed.

rounds.prompt: The passage says the launch of Sputnik 1 changed everything. What changed in the way scientists worked?
choices: They built a model burrow that showed how a rabbit lives inside an animal home.
Scientists began to cooperate across borders, sharing ideas and instruments as they worked towards the Moon.
The sensor had refused to work the day before, so Nora jokes that it tells them nothing at all.
rounds.answer: Scientists began to cooperate across borders, sharing ideas and instruments as they worked towards the Moon.
rounds.explanation: Cooperation across borders is the change the writer names in the sentence straight after the 1957 launch.

rounds.prompt: The prefix mis in the word misunderstood tells you the action was done in which way?
rounds.answer: wrongly
rounds.explanation: The prefix mis means wrongly, so misunderstood means understood wrongly. The prefix re means again.

rounds.prompt: What are people doing when they take part in a boycott?
choices: Refusing to buy or use something to show they disagree

Telling everybody a piece of important news
rounds.answer: Refusing to buy or use something to show they disagree
rounds.explanation: A boycott is a peaceful refusal to buy or use something. The other options describe hoisting, signing a contract and announcing.
